cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A PersistentVolume (PV) is a real piece of storage; a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is an app's request for a size and access mode. Kubernetes binds them, matching a pre-created PV or dynamically provisioning one through a StorageClass, so data survives a Pod being deleted or rescheduled.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: For distributed databases each replica usually gets its own PVC and PV, often via a StatefulSet. Storage gives durability, not distribution: replication, sharding, failover and consistency are the database's job. hostPath ties data to one node, so production uses network or cloud-backed storage.

questions.q: Does deleting a PVC always delete the data?
questions.a: No. It depends on the PV reclaim policy. Delete removes the underlying storage; Retain keeps it.

questions.q: Does a persistent volume make a database highly available?
questions.a: No. It only provides durability. Replication, leader election and failover belong to the database itself.

questions.q: Why is hostPath risky for databases?
questions.a: Data sits on one node's filesystem, so if the Pod moves to another node the data does not follow.
